title: Quickstarts Bootcamp — Recipe Jam (Mar 02 2026)
body:
Context:
This doc captures notes from the "Recipe Jam" we ran during the Quickstarts Bootcamp on 2026-03-02. Goal: produce 3 minimal, high-impact quickstart recipes (Node server, TypeScript client, Dockerized sample) that are copy-paste runnable and demonstrate recommended production settings (streaming, retries, error handling, knobbed batching).

Attendees:
- Claire Nguyen (lead)
- Arjun Patel (samples engineer)
- Maya Thompson (docs, UX)
- Liam O'Connell (SDK maintainer)
- Zoe Martinez (solutions engineer)

Agenda:
1) Quick survey of pain points from field (5m)
2) Pick three recipe targets and split into pairs (10m)
3) Build-time: iterate live and capture commands/snippets (60m)
4) Quick UX pass on README + one-pager checklist (15m)
5) Ship plan + CI tasks (10m)

Field pain points we heard (bullet rough notes):
- quickstarts too chatty — first-run path is buried under explanation
- Node example doesn't show streaming or cancel semantics; users copy naive polling loops
- TypeScript types missing for responses; TS users drop into any which hurts DX
- Docker sample image >1GB; no small variant for demos / container registries are slow in some regions
- CI for sample publish is manual; no nightly smoke test that runs quickstarts end-to-end
- env variable names inconsistent across samples (API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY vs RW_API_TOKEN)

Decisions made during jam:
- Standardize on env var: REDWOOD_API_KEY (documented in root README). Backfill aliases for compatibility (log deprecation in 2 releases).
- Every quickstart must include a "first-run checklist" with exactly 5 commands: install, set env, run, example request, stop/cleanup. Keep it terminal-first.
- Streaming example: Node server will show server-sent events style stream with explicit cancel + server-side cleanup hook. Add minimal backpressure note.
- TypeScript quickstart: publish a types-only package in mono-repo (path: /packages/quickstart-types) and add a small tsconfig that enforces strict types for responses.
- Docker image: two variants — demo (slim, ~250MB) using distroless+multi-stage, and full-dev for local debugging. Use alpine base and build args to control size.

Concrete recipes we committed to produce (owners & rough ETA):
1) Node Streaming Server (Claire + Arjun) — target: simple express server that proxies Redwood API streaming responses, demonstrates cancel token, shows KV cache header guidance. ETA: 2026-03-09
2) TypeScript Client Quickstart (Liam + Maya) — target: minimal TS client that consumes typed responses, example chat + function calling. Include npm script to run typecheck example. ETA: 2026-03-12
3) Dockerized Todo App (Zoe + Arjun) — target: tiny single-container app showing how to run with pinned model, memory limits, and healthcheck. Add small Dockerfile and docker-compose for local dev. ETA: 2026-03-16

Live notes / fragments captured during pairing (raw, unedited):
- Claire: "we should show both streaming and non-streaming path; pick one as default in README — streaming is 'advanced' but important"
- Arjun: quickstart npm scripts: "start, smoke, clean". smoke runs e2e that posts a small prompt and checks for 200 + token count < 1000.
- Liam: TS types: "we can't leak internal fields; we should map model response to stable interface: {id, text, chunks[], usage?} - optional usage flag"
- Maya: README: upfront TL;DR (1-2 lines), then first-run checklist, then reasoning. Keep screenshots optional.
- Zoe: Docker: push to ghcr for demo; small note about regional registry latencies in APAC.

Outstanding issues / open questions:
- Quickstart CI: where to run smoke tests? Consider GitHub Actions with matrix for node versions (18,20) and small ephemeral token (use sandbox account). Provide credentials via Actions secrets. (Jira DX-412)
- Telemetry & PII: do samples send logs? Ensure we call out that quickstarts do not send customer data to Redwood telemetry; add snippet to opt-out env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false
- E2E flakiness: token limits can cause non-deterministic outputs. For smoke tests, pin to short prompts and assert on status + presence of expected token substring rather than full content match.

Action items (clear owners + single-line commitments):
- Claire: scaffold Node streaming repo in mono-repo under examples/node-streaming; create PR with README skeleton by 2026-03-05. (in progress)
- Arjun: implement smoke script and add GH Actions workflow template for samples smoke tests by 2026-03-08. (todo)
- Liam: publish quickstart-types package draft and add types to TS quickstart by 2026-03-10. (todo)
- Maya: author canonical README template and TL;DR checklist; run template over existing quickstarts and note mismatches by 2026-03-09. (todo)
- Zoe: prototype Docker multi-stage Dockerfile and test slim image size; add instructions for GHCR publishing by 2026-03-14. (todo)
- All: add one-line "field note" to each sample that calls out expected cost characteristics (tokens per sample, typical latency). (todo)

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick follow-up async update to be posted in #devexp-quickstarts with PR links and checklist by 2026-03-06.
- Short pairing session for CI template review on 2026-03-08 10:00 PST (30m). Slack invite: @devexp-quickstarts.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep samples as minimal as possible; many users open README then close. Should show "copy this 3 lines" prominently.
- Consider a small video screencast for Node streaming flow (30–60s). Might be produced later if adoption warrants.
- File names: use uniform naming: quickstart-<lang>-<capability>-v1 (e.g. quickstart-node-streaming-v1). Version bumps only for breaking changes.

Links referenced during jam:
- GH PR stub: github:repo/redwood-quickstarts/pull/58
- Jira task: DX-412 (sample smoke tests)
- README template draft: confluence:Quickstart-Playbook-Overview

End of notes.

-- Claire
